steps.name: QC and DESeq2 2x2 interaction model
steps.question: In the WT-vs-KO by vehicle-vs-drug factorial, which genes show a drug response in WT, which show a drug response in KO, and which show a significantly different drug response between genotypes (genotype:treatment interaction)?

grounding.reason: Standard DESeq2 2x2 factorial with interaction term; no knowledge_recommend service was attached to this run.

steps.description: Load the salmon gene-level counts (12,000 genes x 17-column CSV, first column gene symbol) and the 16-row metadata (genotype, treatment, condition), verify sample alignment and that condition matches the genotype:treatment combination, run sample-level QC (library size, PCA on variance-stabilized counts, replicate concordance within the four 2x2 cells), then fit a single DESeq2 model with design ~ genotype + treatment + genotype:treatment and extract: (1) drug effect in WT (drug - vehicle | WT), (2) drug effect in KO (drug - vehicle | KO), (3) the interaction contrast (KO drug effect minus WT drug effect), which directly answers the research question. Apply BH correction and apeglm LFC shrinkage for effect-size reporting. Reference data: none required.
acceptance_criteria: Counts matrix (12,000 genes x 16 samples) and metadata (16 rows: genotype, treatment, condition) load; all 16 sample names match 1:1 between files and metadata genotype/treatment values are consistent with the combined condition column
QC report: per-sample library sizes, gene detection, sample outliers flagged, PCA colored by genotype and by treatment
DESeq2 fits design ~ genotype + treatment + genotype:treatment with size-factor normalization and dispersion estimation

Three contrast tables produced: drug vs vehicle within WT, drug vs vehicle within KO, and interaction (KO drug effect minus WT drug effect), each with log2FC, shrunken log2FC (apeglm), SE, Wald p-value, BH-adjusted p-value, baseMean
Results written as TSVs; number of significant genes per contrast at padj<0.05 reported, with the caveat that n=4 per cell gives limited power for the interaction term

steps.name: Visualization of contrasts and interaction
steps.question: How do the drug effects in WT and KO compare gene-by-gene, and which genes drive the interaction?

grounding.reason: Standard DE visualization; no knowledge_recommend service was attached to this run.

steps.description: From the fitted model and VST-transformed counts of T1S1, produce: PCA colored by genotype and by treatment; volcano plots for the WT drug effect, KO drug effect, and interaction contrasts with top genes labeled; a scatter plot of the WT drug log2FC against the KO drug log2FC (deviation from the diagonal is the interaction) highlighting interaction-significant genes; and a z-scaled heatmap of the top interaction genes annotated by genotype and treatment.
acceptance_criteria: PCA of VST counts colored by genotype and treatment saved
Volcano plots for all three contrasts saved
Scatter of WT drug log2FC vs KO drug log2FC with interaction-significant genes highlighted saved
Heatmap of top interaction genes (VST, z-scaled, annotated by genotype/treatment) saved

steps.name: Pathway enrichment of drug-response contrasts
steps.question: Are the genes whose drug response differs between KO and WT (and the per-genotype drug responses) enriched for known biological pathways?

grounding.reason: Standard fgsea preranked GSEA; no knowledge_recommend service was attached to this run.

steps.description: Run fgsea preranked GSEA against the staged WikiPathways Homo sapiens GMT (HGNC gene symbols, matching the count matrix rows) on three ranked lists: the interaction Wald statistic, the WT drug-effect statistic, and the KO drug-effect statistic. Report per-pathway size after intersection with the 12,000 measured genes, NES, and BH-adjusted p-values. This step is hypothesis-generating: with n=4 per cell the underlying rankings are noisy. Reference data: a WikiPathways human pathway GMT (gene sets as HGNC symbols); if absent, report the gap and skip enrichment rather than substitute another species' gene sets.
acceptance_criteria: Gene sets resolved from the staged human WikiPathways GMT, intersected with the 12,000 measured gene symbols; intersection sizes reported per pathway
fgsea run on three ranked lists: interaction statistic, drug effect in WT, drug effect in KO
Results tables with pathway, size, NES, p-value, padj written as TSVs; if the GMT is absent the step reports that and writes an empty result instead of failing

plan.title: Drug x genotype interaction DE in 2x2 factorial
plan.analytical_narrative: The question 'does the drug act differently in knockout than in wild type?' is formally the genotype-by-treatment interaction in a 2x2 factorial (WT/KO x vehicle/drug, n=4 per cell, 16 human brain bulk RNA-seq samples, 12,000 genes from salmon). The analysis therefore centers on a single DESeq2 model with design ~ genotype + treatment + genotype:treatment, from which three contrasts are extracted: the drug effect within WT, the drug effect within KO, and the interaction (difference of drug effects). A separate model without the interaction term cannot answer the question, so it is not used for inference. Given only 4 replicates per cell, the interaction test is inherently low-powered, so the plan pairs p-values with effect sizes and empirical-Bayes shrunken log2FCs, and treats pathway-level results on the interaction signature as hypothesis-generating. QC (library sizes, PCA, replicate concordance) precedes modeling; volcano/MA/heatmap visualization follows; the interaction and per-genotype drug-response rankings are finally tested against WikiPathways human gene sets (staged reference, HGNC symbols matching the count matrix rows) with fgsea.
